constants.description: Age of the universe for the base-ΛCDM model, 68% interval. From Planck 2018 VI, Table 2, column TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO (the 13.787 ± 0.020 Gyr figure). The baseline Planck-only column TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing gives 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr.

citation.text: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6 (Planck 2018 results VI), Table 2, TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO

constants.description: Temperature of the cosmic microwave background today, from the review of all published measurements in Fixsen (2009), stated in the abstract.

Redshift z* of last scattering (photon decoupling at recombination), base-ΛCDM, 68% interval. Planck 2018 VI, Table 2, column TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO; the same column as universe.age. The baseline column without BAO gives 1089.92 ± 0.25.

citation.text: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6 (Planck 2018 results VI), Table 2, TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO

constants.description: Approximate age of the universe at last scattering, shown as the widely quoted round figure. Its origin is the WMAP first-year best fit, t_dec = 379 (+8, −7) kyr (Bennett et al. 2003, Table 3). Current values are slightly lower: the PDG 2026 Big-Bang Cosmology review (Sec. 22.4.1) gives about 370,000 years, and integrating the Friedmann equation with the Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO parameters to z* = 1089.80 gives about 372,000 years. Flagged for the science reviewer.

citation.text: Bennett et al. 2003, ApJS 148, 1 (WMAP first-year results), Table 3; compare PDG 2026, Review 22 (Big-Bang Cosmology), Sec. 22.4.1

constants.description: Approximate temperature of the radiation at last scattering, derived as T* = T0 × (1 + z*) = 2.72548 K × 1090.80 ≈ 2,973 K (T0 from cmb.temperature, z* from recombination.redshift), shown rounded to about 3,000 K.

citation.text: Derived from Fixsen 2009 (ApJ 707, 916) and Planck Collaboration 2020 (A&A 641, A6), Table 2

constants.description: Primordial helium-4 mass fraction Y_P, inferred from metal-poor extragalactic H II regions; the PDG recommended value, eq. (24.3).

citation.text: Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026 (Takahashi et al., Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 41, 2630011), eq. (24.3)

constants.description: Primordial hydrogen mass fraction, derived as X = 1 − Y_P = 1 − 0.245 = 0.755. Deuterium, helium-3 and lithium-7 together are below 0.01% by mass and are neglected; the uncertainty is that of Y_P.

citation.text: Derived from Y_P in Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, eq. (24.3)

constants.description: Fraction of primordial atoms that are helium, derived from Y_P = 0.245 ± 0.003. With atomic masses m(4He)/m(1H) = 4.00260325413 / 1.00782503223 = 3.97153 (NIST), He/H by number = (Y_P / 3.97153) / (1 − Y_P) = 0.08171, so f_He = 0.08171 / 1.08171 = 0.07554. Error propagation: df/dY = f(1 − f) / (Y(1 − Y)) = 0.3775, times 0.003 gives ± 0.0011. Trace nuclei neglected.

citation.text: Derived from Y_P in Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, eq. (24.3), with NIST atomic masses

constants.description: Fraction of primordial atoms that are hydrogen: 1 − f_He = 1 − 0.0755 = 0.9245 (see bbn.helium.numberFraction for the derivation). Trace nuclei neglected.

citation.text: Derived from Y_P in Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, eq. (24.3), with NIST atomic masses

constants.description: Primordial deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio by number, D/H = (25.08 ± 0.29) × 10^-6: the PDG recommended value from quasar absorption systems, eq. (24.2).

citation.text: Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, eq. (24.2)

constants.description: Primordial lithium-7-to-hydrogen ratio by number inferred from metal-poor halo stars, Li/H = (1.45 ± 0.25) × 10^-10, eq. (24.4). The review notes it should be regarded as a lower bound, since stars may have destroyed some of their lithium.
constants.qualifier: observed in old stars; regarded as a lower bound

citation.text: Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, eq. (24.4)

constants.description: Lithium-7-to-hydrogen ratio calculated from standard Big-Bang nucleosynthesis with the CMB baryon density, Li/H = (4.72 ± 0.7) × 10^-10, eq. (24.10) (the review's reference [45]).

citation.text: Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, eq. (24.10)

constants.description: Factor by which the calculated (standard BBN) primordial lithium-7 abundance exceeds the value observed in old stars (the cosmological lithium problem): a factor of 3.3, a 4.4 sigma discrepancy, Sec. 24.5.

citation.text: Fields, Molaro & Sarkar, Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis, Review 24 in PDG 2026, Sec. 24.5
